transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas. That $6,500,000 peak two-hour net settlement outflow is critical context for what I need to share on collateral. While reviewing our collateral inventory this week, I confirmed that exactly $4,000,000 of unencumbered Treasury bills are eligible for the rail's liquidity facility. I should note two things: first, there appears to be a gap between the $6.5 million projected peak outflow and the $4 million in eligible collateral we currently have identified. Second, our liquidity-risk policy requires a daily eligibility and substitution check on this collateral, and the inventory note documenting this $4 million figure has not yet been attached to the operating-plan file. Maya, I want to flag this funding gap for your awareness as you consider sign-off, and I recommend we formally escalate the $2.5 million shortfall for resolution after this meeting rather than blocking the current sign-off decision, consistent with our review process.

transcript.text: Thank you, Maya. On monitoring from payments operations, our real-time settlement monitoring dashboard is configured and ready for the September 1st activation. We have alerts set for threshold breaches on net settlement positions, and we'll be monitoring intraday flows continuously during business hours. The dashboard will flag any position approaching our settlement limits so we can coordinate with treasury on funding actions. From my side, I'm comfortable with the monitoring setup and ready to support the operating plan submission. I don't have any additional monitoring requirements beyond what I've already described.

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas. From the liquidity risk side on monitoring, our requirements complement what Jonas has described. We need to ensure that the daily eligibility and substitution check on our rail-eligible collateral is integrated into the monitoring framework — this is a policy requirement I flagged earlier. Specifically, we need a daily confirmation that the $4 million in unencumbered Treasury bills remains eligible and unencumbered, with any substitution documented and reflected in the operating-plan file. Additionally, given the $2.5 million funding gap I identified, I'd recommend that our monitoring setup include an alert tied to collateral adequacy — not just settlement position thresholds — so that treasury is notified promptly if the gap is not resolved before activation or if collateral eligibility changes. Beyond that, I'm comfortable with the monitoring setup as Jonas has described it, and I'm ready to support the operating plan submission with the formal escalation of the shortfall for post-meeting resolution.
